answers.answer: 1. Starting money: each player takes 25. 2. Workers: one association worker starts active on the notepad and three start inactive/lying down below it. 3. Zoo cards: draw 8, keep 4 and discard 4 face up. 4. Final Scoring cards: draw 2 and keep them hidden. 5. Action cards: place side I of all five; Animals goes in slot 1 and the other four are randomized among slots 2–5. 6. Starting appeal by turn order: first player space 0, second space 1, third space 2, fourth space 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup B–F: Animals under leftmost slot; take 25 money; draw 2 Final Scoring cards; draw 8 and keep 4; appeal staggered by turn order.

answers.answer: 1. Base projects: place 4 face up below the Association board in a four-player game; in two- or three-player games place 3. 2. Two players: block the left level on the left project, middle level on the middle project, right level on the right project, and the three spaces in the donation area's left column; these are unusable by either player. 3. Three or four players: no project levels or donation spaces are blocked at setup. 4. Initial display: reveal its 6 cards only after every player has chosen their opening hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c and G: four projects in 4 players, otherwise three; 2-player blocking; reveal display after hand selection.

answers.answer: 1. After using slot 4, remove that card, shift cards that were to its left one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Fix strength before the action; each X-token spent beforehand adds +1, and tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. 3. Any number of X-tokens may be spent, but you may hold at most 5; some actions stop benefiting above strength 5. 4. Resolve an ‘after finishing’ effect only after completing the action and moving its card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: remove the card, shift cards left of empty slot right, used card to slot 1; X-token strength set before; after-finishing effects after movement.

answers.answer: 1. You may not take a regular action that does nothing; you must play at least one animal or build at least one building when choosing those actions. 2. Instead, select any Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; its slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3. Move the selected card to slot 1, shifting intervening cards right. 4. You cannot take this alternative if you already hold 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘You may not do nothing’; X-token action states exactly 1, card movement, and five-token limit.

answers.answer: 1. When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore further movement beyond the end. 2. The player who reached it gains 1 X-token. 3. Finish the triggering player's current turn; the break occurs afterward. 4. After the break, play continues clockwise with the next player; the Break token resets to the player-count starting space.
answers.evidence: Break track: last space calls break after current turn, grants 1 X-token, ignores extra steps; token resets after break.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I first advances the Break token 2 spaces without money, then choose either deck draw by its strength table (up to 3, with any required discard) or a snap of exactly 1 display card at strength 5+. 2. Cards II also advances 2, then may draw from the deck and/or take cards from within reputation range in any order according to its table. 3. Snap thresholds: I needs strength 5; II needs 3, and strength above 3 adds nothing to a snap. A snap on either side takes exactly one display card of any reputation and does not also draw from the deck. 4. Reputation range restricts only Cards II's display-draw choice, not snapping. 5. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. 6. Hand limit is checked only at breaks, when discarding to 3 cards or 5 with the hand-limit university.
answers.evidence: CARDS action: both sides advance 2; snap rules and range restriction; Special Rules: end-of-turn display refill, hand size enforced at breaks.

answers.answer: 1. ‘Within reputation range’ means the display card in the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires upgraded Cards II. 3. At reputation 15, further reputation does not move the counter; gain 1 appeal for each excess reputation step. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display: range definition, 10+ requires upgraded Cards, overflow at 15 becomes appeal; discard pile may not be inspected.

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly 1 building up to action strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, but not two identical buildings in one action. 2. Buildings cost 2 money per space, paid before placement. 3. First building must include at least one border space; later buildings must share an edge with an existing building. 4. Build only on empty map spaces; buildings cannot overlap, extend off-map, or cover water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 5. Every kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion gives 1 appeal immediately, once.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: exactly one vs different buildings/total size; placement rules, kiosk spacing, costs; pavilion increases appeal by 1.

answers.answer: 1. Build I permits standard enclosures, kiosk, pavilion and one Petting Zoo per zoo. 2. Build II additionally permits Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary; each is a size-5 special enclosure, and a zoo may have at most one of each special type. 3. There are four tiles of each special-enclosure type in the supply, one for each player. 4. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter only through Sponsor cards. 5. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 appeal; this may be achieved by any effect, though restricted spaces require Build II to build on them.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build table and text: Build I/II availability, max one each, four tiles each; unique buildings via Sponsors; full map gives 7 appeal.

answers.answer: 1. Earlier benefits gained within an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used in later steps of that action; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. 2. Thus a prior gain can fund a later building, animal or task, but money/effects from an item cannot pay that item's own cost. 3. Ordinary effects resolve immediately; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the whole action is complete and its Action card has moved. 4. For simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens: earlier action bonuses can be used later, pay before benefits; ‘after finishing’ effects after movement; simultaneous effects order chosen by owner.

answers.answer: 1. Check all left-side play conditions, pay the printed cost, and house the animal legally; you cannot play a card whose conditions are unmet. 2. A partner zoo matching the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon on that animal, including a double icon. Pay the full adjusted cost before money-gain effects from the play. 3. A standard enclosure must be empty and at least the animal's required size; the animal normally goes alone there and the whole tile flips to occupied. Petting Zoo animals must use the Petting Zoo. 4. Eligible reptiles and some birds may instead use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary if the animal's marked capacity fits; place one supply player token per required space and never flip a special enclosure. 5. Required water/rock adjacency applies to the chosen housing, including special enclosures; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes, not multiple touching edges to the same hex, and meet the printed one/two-space requirement. 6. Appeal and ordinary effects resolve during play; an ‘after finishing’ effect waits until all animals are played and the Animals card has moved. When playing two, finish the first animal's steps before the second.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action: conditions, adjusted cost, housing, terrain and effect order; ‘Money-gain timing’ and enclosure state table.

answers.answer: 1. Animals II permits playing Animal cards from the display within reputation range as well as from hand; for each display card pay its folder number in addition to other costs. 2. At strength 5 or more, you may optionally gain 1 reputation at the very beginning, so the increased range applies to animals played in that action. 3. Do not replenish the display until the turn ends. 4. Animals II permits animal cards whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS Side II paragraph: display, folder cost, optional reputation first, no refill until turn end, upgrade-required conditions.

answers.answer: 1. Existing animals may move only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built, and only corresponding animals eligible for that building; consider each animal separately and move all suitable animals that fit. 2. Capacity is marked by adding the animal's indicated number of player tokens from your supply to the new special enclosure; its full capacity must be available, and terrain adjacency must be met. 3. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all that animal's requirements, including terrain. 4. If none meets all requirements, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even size, flip none. The animal still moves if special-enclosure capacity and terrain requirements permit.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals section: only at construction, eligible animals, tokens, and smallest-enclosure fallback.

answers.answer: 1. Association task strengths: reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, conservation project 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task with action strength at least that task's value. Association II performs one or more different tasks with total task value no greater than its strength. 3. Place one active worker on a task; if one of your workers is already there, place two instead; with three of yours already there, you cannot repeat before the break. 4. Other players' workers on that task do not matter.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action: task strength list, sides I/II, workers required when repeating, opponents' workers irrelevant.

answers.answer: 1. Partner zoos and universities are taken from available tiles on the Association board and placed on the lowest empty corresponding space of your zoo map. Resolve any covered-space bonus immediately; for a university also take its own printed reputation reward immediately. 2. Partner zoos must be from different continents; maximum 4, with the third and fourth requiring Association II. Universities cannot be duplicated. 3. A partner zoo provides its continent icon and reduces animal costs from that continent by 3 per continent icon. 4. Only the hand-limit university raises the break hand limit from 3 to 5; other universities leave it at 3.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION tasks and University tiles table: board tiles, placement/rewards, distinct continents, partner cap/upgrades, no duplicate university, hand limit.

answers.answer: 1. Association I can support an existing project or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately. Association II can also use a display project within reputation range, paying its folder number; do not refill until turn end. A new card enters the leftmost space above the Association board and pushes others right. 2. To support, fulfill a printed condition and choose an unoccupied reward level; each level holds only one player's token total, and you normally support each project at most once. 3. Take a player token from the left edge of your zoo map and put it on the chosen condition. Gain the depicted reward and activate the uncovered map bonus immediately; choose either order for the project reward and immediate map bonus. 4. When a new project exceeds the player-count display limit, discard the rightmost project; its tokens return to their owners' supplies and activated map bonuses remain. Base projects below the board never move or replenish.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work: sources, enter play, overflow, support limits/procedure, map-bonus payment timing.

answers.answer: 1. Match the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement to the Release project category: 2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. The occupied enclosure tile or special-enclosure capacity does not change that category; another animal category cannot substitute. 2. Before gaining conservation, lose only that animal's printed appeal, discard it and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and effects already earned. 3. If it could live in a special enclosure and the required tokens can be removed, remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, including terrain. If none does, flip the smallest meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. This applies to flock animals too. 4. Playing a new Release project gives its player 1 reputation; later support of an existing one does not.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild projects: size categories; appeal/icons and retained gains; special tokens and enclosure fallback; new-card reputation.

answers.answer: 1. Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand if action strength is at least its level and its conditions are met, or advances the Break token by strength and takes that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play one or more from hand and/or in-range display; strength +1 must cover total levels, and each display card costs its folder number extra. Resolve cards sequentially, finishing each card's instant effects before the next; defer after-finishing effects until the action ends. 3. If using the money option, advance by strength and take money twice the strength. Even if only one break-track step remains, the full amount is paid; excess movement is ignored at the track end.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action: I strength and full money; II budget/sources/order/double money; Side I money full even if break track needs fewer steps.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit; clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock partner zoos/universities except kinds every player owns; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Hand limit is 3 normally or 5 with the hand-limit university. 3. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, while empty special enclosures do. 4. For players receiving display cards during income, resolve them clockwise beginning with the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise); refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses. This ordering/refill rule applies together.
answers.evidence: Break procedure steps 1–6; kiosk income list; display-card ordering and refill stated in income step.

answers.answer: 1. At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate one more association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus tile beside that space; execute/remove a chosen tile, while the money option remains if tiles run out. At 10, the first player reaching it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile. 2. Check the end only at the end of your own turn or during a break, when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or have passed one another. If appeal is gained during another player's turn, its owner waits until their own turn ends or a break to check. 3. On an end trigger at a player's turn end, that player finishes and every other player gets one more turn; if triggered during a break, everyone gets one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can add at most 4 conservation points. VP = appeal minus the lowest appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive VP wins; tie goes to most supported projects, then tied players share victory.
answers.evidence: Conservation track rewards, End of game and Final scoring sections.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the 9 Bonus tiles, place one face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track (two beside 5 and two beside 8), and return the other five to the box. Do not put tiles on the two yellow icon spaces. 2. Components: if a component runs out, use a suitable substitute; stock alone does not prevent a legal play, though explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability still apply.
answers.evidence: Global setup step 2; Component supply: use a suitable substitute if a component runs out.

answers.answer: 1. Maps 1–8 are advanced maps on reverse sides, each with an individual ability. Either take two random zoo maps and choose one advanced map, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse order of play; return unselected maps. 2. Map A starts with an empty size-3 enclosure and a kiosk on indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built and gets a tile reminder.
answers.evidence: Personal setup A: advanced-map selection methods; Map A ability places empty 3-space enclosure and kiosk.

answers.answer: 1. The seven player tokens used for conservation support start on the designated spaces at the left edge of each zoo map. 2. Hire/activate inactive workers from the lowest space upward. 3. Some maps grant conservation points when you hire your last worker; Full-throated also awards any such printed map reward.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2; Special Rules: hire from lowest supply space upward and last-worker reward; Full-throated clarification.

answers.answer: 1. On an upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to II and leave it in its current slot. 2. The improved action is available starting with your next action, but it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. 3. No: there are four upgrade opportunities and one allows an alternative, so you cannot upgrade all five cards.
answers.evidence: Upgrading Action cards: stays in slot, next action, immediate condition status, four ways and cannot upgrade all.

answers.answer: 1. Cards I draw/discard at strengths 1–5: 1/1, 1/0, 2/1, 2/0, 3/1 respectively. 2. A required discard may be one of the newly drawn cards or a card already in your hand.
answers.evidence: Cards draw tables and note: required discard may be newly drawn or previously held.

answers.answer: 1. The seven animal categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. Bears count as a category even when their icon appears alongside herbivore or predator; Petting Zoo animal is its own category. Include both unless the effect explicitly excludes them.
answers.evidence: Animal categories (7); Base glossary: shared principles.

answers.answer: 1. Donation requires upgraded Association II and at least one association task performed in that same action; it needs no worker and is limited to one donation per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible, cover that donation space with a player token from your supply, and gain 1 conservation. 3. Ladder: 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, later donations cost 12 and place no additional token. 4. In two-player setup, the left donation column is blocked for both players.
answers.evidence: Donations—Association II only: eligibility, pay/reward, cost ladder, final space; setup 5c blocking.

answers.answer: 1. Count Animal- and Sponsor-card upper-right icons; also count water/rock requirements in the upper-left on Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards. Count partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions or Conservation Project icons; a university's reputation reward and hand-limit symbol are not zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icons for its effects; doubled icons count twice. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo; university icon note; Card text takes priority.

answers.answer: 1. For two water/rock spaces, count distinct adjacent terrain hexes; several edges touching the same hex count once, and in a larger region count only hexes actually adjacent to the building. 2. Water/rock illustrations printed on tiles are not terrain spaces and do not satisfy requirements. The summary does not state a separate terrain-connectivity requirement for this animal adjacency test.
answers.evidence: Animal housing: count distinct adjacent hexes; terrain illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

answers.answer: 1. The player who plays a new Release into the Wild project receives 1 reputation; a player who later supports a project already in play does not receive that play bonus. 2. All Breeding Program project cards have the same requirement at all three reward spaces on that card; when the condition is met, choose any available reward space.
answers.evidence: Release projects: playing new project grants reputation; ALL Breeding Program cards same requirement/all available space choice.

answers.answer: 1. In an X:Y effect, X is the condition and Y the reward. 2. A condition without a number, or with ‘per,’ pays once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; if there are several thresholds, use the highest one met.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: ‘For an effect written X : Y…’

answers.answer: 1. Connected means uncovered and sharing an edge with a covered space. 2. Isolated means a space with no adjacent covered space. 3. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes those for all players.
answers.evidence: Base glossary definitions of connected, isolated, border, your zoo and any zoo.

answers.answer: 1. A unique building enters play through its Sponsor card and must be placed when that card is played; if it cannot be legally placed, the Sponsor cannot be played. 2. Use the matching tile, colored face up; rotate freely but do not flip. 3. Follow ordinary placement and shown terrain-adjacency rules; no size-based building payment is due. 4. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house additional animals, and never count as terrain spaces. 5. Therefore, if the tile cannot fit legally, you cannot play its Sponsor card.
answers.evidence: Base glossary: Unique buildings must be placed when playing their Sponsor; placement, orientation, payment and enclosure/terrain rules.

answers.answer: 1. For both a named Action and Determination, finish the Animals action and move the Animals card before performing the granted action. 2. Use that action's Action card normally; after the granted action, move that card to slot 1 normally. 3. A named Action must be performed as named and cannot be replaced with X-token action. Determination (Any Action) may choose any action, including the X-token alternative.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications—Action/Determination: shared timing and movement; named Action vs Any Action.

answers.answer: 1. Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds its chosen project to hand; Dominance takes its named project from that deck. 2. Dominance has no effect if that named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediately support the acquired base card through Association, placing it above the board; it does not join the setup base-project row below.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications—Assertion / Dominance.

answers.answer: 1. Both Boost and Clever resolve after finishing Animals and moving the Animals card. 2. Clever puts the chosen Action card in slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. 3. Boost puts the named card in slot 1 or slot 5; moving it to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications—Boost / Clever.

answers.answer: 1. Every affected zoo needs at least 5 appeal for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering 1, each of Pilfering 2's two target selections, and Constriction. Check the floor separately for each selection. 2. The played animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so its new appeal normally need not count when selecting the affected zoo. 3. In multiplayer, the group may replace interactive abilities with the solo-marked alternative text without playing solo mode.
answers.evidence: Interactive abilities shared eligibility; target reference; playing animal appeal may be before/after ability; multiplayer alternative text.

answers.answer: 1. Each affected other zoo places Constriction on its own Action cards: if ahead on one track, one token on its slot-5 card; if ahead on both, one token on its slot-4 card and one on its slot-5 card. 2. Never stack two Constriction tokens on a card; return duplicates. 3. Each token reduces that action's strength by 2, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 4. Return a token after using its card, or without effect at the break.
answers.evidence: Constriction target reference and detailed Constriction rules.

answers.answer: 1. At effective strength zero or below, you may spend enough X-tokens to reach at least 1 strength. 2. Alternatively, take the X-token alternative action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. 3. The X-token alternative still follows its normal limit: unavailable if already holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Constriction: at effective strength zero or below, boost to one, use alternative, or wait until slot 3; X-token action limit.

answers.answer: 1. Yes. With Digging 2, choose again after each of up to two selections between discarding a display card and replenishing it, or discarding a hand card then drawing one deck card. 2. A display discard through Digging is replaced immediately: shift higher folders down and draw into folder 6.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications—Digging 2 / Digging.

answers.answer: 1. A flock animal avoids flipping a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo has a printed standard size at least as large as the flock animal's requirement. 2. The same qualifying herbivore may host any number of flock animals. 3. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. 4. On release, you need not prove the historical accommodation or track which animal was its original host; apply the ordinary release procedure, which frees an occupied enclosure under its fallback rules.
answers.evidence: Flock Animal clarification: qualifying herbivore, repeated host, later non-flock restriction, no historical tracking/release procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take any conservation-point reward printed on your map for hiring your last worker. 3. If all workers are already active, the ability has no effect.
answers.evidence: Full-throated clarification.

answers.answer: 1. If Hunter reveals no Animal card, discard all revealed cards; you add no card to hand.
answers.evidence: Hunter X: with no Animal among revealed cards, discard all.

answers.answer: 1. Choose among tied players for highest appeal; if you select yourself, Hypnosis has no effect. 2. Copy only a card in the target's slot 1, 2 or 3, using its owner's upgraded/unupgraded side for the whole copied action; other action-card upgrade checks use your own cards. 3. You may spend your own X-tokens. Venom and Constriction tokens on the copied card affect you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. 4. Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally. 5. For copied permissions, the target card's side applies to the copied action (e.g. Build II restrictions, Animals II upgrade-conditioned animals); Association I still has its two-partner limit even if your Association is II. Unique building placement from borrowed Sponsors checks your own Build side.
answers.evidence: Hypnosis detailed rules: tie/self target, slot, side, X-tokens, token treatment, movement and borrowed permissions.

answers.answer: 1. Place a gained Multiplier immediately: on its named Action card if the reward names one; for a Bonus tile, choose any card, including Animals. 2. On its next use, the action may execute twice in succession at the same base strength; move the card only after both executions. Each additional used Multiplier adds one execution, so two allow up to three actions. 3. X-tokens boost only one execution. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions end. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the entire turn is finished; it cannot stop the second execution. 4. Return used tokens to supply; remove an unused token at the next break.
answers.evidence: Multiplier table and rules: placement, executions, X-token use, timing, break wait, return.

answers.answer: 1. Two Multiplier tokens on one card provide up to three executions total, not four. 2. Different permitted choices may be made in each regular execution. 3. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but you may not mix an X-token action with a regular action in the same multiplication.
answers.evidence: Multiplier: additional multipliers; choices; multiplied X-token alternative and no mixing.

answers.answer: 1. Peacocking lets you place the Large Bird Aviary before Build II, provided your zoo does not already have one and a legal site exists. 2. Other normal placement rules still apply, including Build II for restricted-icon map spaces. 3. Posturing follows normal placement and kiosk spacing; place multiple buildings one at a time.
answers.evidence: Peacocking and Posturing clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. The first Petting Zoo animal gives 3 appeal, the second 6, and the third 9. 2. The single Petting Zoo holds at most three such animals. 3. They count as small animals.
answers.evidence: Petting Zoo animal clarification.

answers.answer: 1. For both Pilfering 1 and each of Pilfering 2's selections, the acting player chooses the affected zoo among tied leaders. Pilfering 2 resolves highest appeal and most conservation separately. 2. Each target must have at least 5 appeal; the conservation target also needs at least 1 conservation. If all players have zero conservation, that selection has no effect, while Pilfering 2's appeal selection is still resolved separately. 3. Selecting yourself has no effect; Pilfering 2's other selection resolves normally.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X: tie rule, separate targets, eligibility floor, zero-conservation rule, self-target rule.

answers.answer: 1. The target chooses either to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. 2. If the target has no hand cards, they give 5 money; if they have less than 5 money, they give a card. If they have neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. 3. Resolve repeated Pilferings sequentially; the target may choose differently each time.
answers.evidence: Pilfering X: target choice, no-hand/low-money/neither cases, sequential resolution.

answers.answer: 1. Pouch tucks hand cards under the animal for 2 appeal per card; tucked cards have no remaining function. If the animal is released, discard its tucked cards too, but keep the appeal already earned. 2. Sunbathing sells up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. An extra Final Scoring card drawn by Resistance before the 10-conservation milestone joins the player's choices when discarding one card at that milestone. 2. At game end, score every Final Scoring card remaining; each card is separately capped at 4 conservation points.
answers.evidence: Resistance clarification; Final scoring cap.

answers.answer: 1. Shuffle the discard pile face down, draw randomly from it, make the ability's stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. Scavenging 3 draws three random cards, keeps one and discards the others.
answers.evidence: Scavenging clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; deck draw is not an alternative. 2. Sponsor Magnet takes display Sponsors without a reputation-range restriction; if none are present, nothing happens. 3. Ordinary end-of-turn display refill applies.
answers.evidence: Snapping and Sponsor Magnet clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal than yours that has at least 5 appeal. Put tokens on that zoo's lowest-slot cards first (slot 1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. 2. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn; this includes X-token alternative action if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens. 3. At turn end, pay 2 money only if you removed no Venom token that turn and at least one Venom token remains on your cards. If unable, undo the turn and choose another action; spending all money does not avoid the fee. 4. Unused tokens expire at the next break without effect.
answers.evidence: Venom X detailed rules.

answers.answer: 1. Veterinarian gives 2/5/10 money immediately for 1/2/3 universities. 2. Its recurring effect lowers the required strength for conservation project work to 4 instead of 5. 3. Its final reward is 1 conservation for three universities.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 203 Veterinarian.

answers.answer: 1. Medical Breakthrough's immediate appeal is 2 per previously supported project, counted by player tokens missing from the left edge of the map. 2. It gives 1 conservation at each break.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 206 Medical Breakthrough.

answers.answer: 1. Basic Research counts distinct continent and animal-category icon types together, excluding research; count each type only once even if repeated or doubled. 2. Its owner gains 1 conservation per two distinct types, rounding down. 3. Each other player gains 2 money per conservation point the owner gains.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 207 Basic Research.

answers.answer: 1. Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon immediately. 2. Whenever any player plays a research icon, the Science Library owner gains 2 money. 3. Its final condition is five different animal categories, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 208 Science Library.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on the Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon immediately. 2. Each Americas icon played permits a free kiosk under normal placement and spacing rules. 3. Its final condition is five or more kiosks, granting 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 210 Expert on the Americas.

answers.answer: 1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon immediately. 2. For each Australia icon played, you may tuck one hand card under it for 2 appeal. 3. Tucked cards have no further function.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 212 Expert on Australia.

answers.answer: 1. When played, each of Global Breeding Program and Breeding Program takes two player tokens from your supply and stores them on its two printed top spaces. 2. When supporting a base project below the Association board, return exactly one of that card's tokens to your supply as any one icon; the two tokens cannot both be used for one project. Base-origin project cards later played above the board do not qualify. 3. Final reward: 1 conservation with five or more project supports, counted by missing left-map tokens.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 215/218 Global Breeding Program; Breeding Program.

answers.answer: 1. Engineer allows each Build action to include one extra copy of a building built in that same action without extra strength. 2. Pay its normal money cost and follow placement rules; only one extra building is allowed, and special enclosures retain their one-per-type limit. 3. Final reward: 5 appeal with a full map except water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 217 Engineer.

answers.answer: 1. Diversity Researcher gives 2 money per water/rock icon immediately. 2. Its recurring effect permits covering water/rock spaces and ignoring animal and unique-building terrain requirements; terrain need not be covered for a full map. 3. Once terrain is covered, it stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo. 4. Final scoring gives 2 appeal per water-icon/rock-icon pair, to a maximum of three pairs/6 appeal.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 219 Diversity Researcher.

answers.answer: 1. Each actual placement bonus on a border space triggers Archaeologist's additional choice of any uncovered placement bonus on the map, not necessarily on the border. 2. Multiple border bonuses grant multiple extra choices; copied bonuses may be the same or different, and resolve them in any chosen order. 3. Final condition: all building border spaces covered, excluding water/rock, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 221 Archaeologist.

answers.answer: 1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. Each Release into the Wild support yields 1 additional conservation. 3. You may repeatedly support the same release project using different qualifying animals, but place at most one token on that project per Association action. 4. Each token counts as a separate project support for other effects.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 224 Migration Recording.

answers.answer: 1. Quarantine Lab gives 1 X-token immediately. 2. It makes you immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis and Pilfering, ignore your counters and find the next qualifying player. 3. Its final condition is all five continents, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 225 Quarantine Lab.

answers.answer: 1. Choose small or large permanently and mark that choice with a player token from your supply. Reveal deck cards until an animal of that type appears, keep it and discard the rest. 2. Thereafter you cannot play animals of the opposite type. 3. Chosen small animals gain 2 extra appeal; chosen large animals gain 4. Size-3 animals remain legal but receive no bonus.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 227 WAZA Special Assignment.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal immediately. 2. An Animals action consisting only of small animals qualifies: you may play one additional small animal from hand with normal costs/rules. 3. Then add one small animal from the display to hand regardless of reputation; you may take it even if you declined the extra play. Mixing small and large in the original action prevents the effect.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 228 WAZA Small Animals Program.

answers.answer: 1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon on play. 2. Its recurring effect grants 1 money for each newly covered space adjacent to water, even multiple spaces in one building; a space touching several water hexes still pays only once. 3. Final condition: all water hexes connected, with none isolated, for 1 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 241 Hydrologist.

answers.answer: 1. Barred Owl Hut is a unique building placed when its Sponsor is played; its placement follows the general unique-building rules. 2. Each bird icon played triggers a draw of two deck cards, keep one and discard the other.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 249 Barred Owl Hut; unique-building rules.

answers.answer: 1. Sea Turtle Tank is placed adjacent to water under unique-building rules. 2. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard sold cards.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 250 Sea Turtle Tank.

answers.answer: 1. Spotted Hyena Compound triggers Hunter whenever a predator icon is played, with draws equal to your total predator icons. 2. If one newly played card has a double-predator icon, it triggers two sequential Hunters; count both new icons each time.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 252 Spotted Hyena Compound.

answers.answer: 1. Okapi Stable enters play with three supply player tokens on its card. 2. For each herbivore icon played, you may spend one token and pay money equal to a Sponsor card in hand's level to play that Sponsor, subject to its normal conditions. 3. The Stable's own herbivore icon can trigger this when it is played; it has three total uses. The Sponsor source is hand.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 253 Okapi Stable.

answers.answer: 1. Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation immediately. 2. Place its unique building covering at least two border spaces. 3. Take one display card within reputation range or draw one deck card. Resolve simultaneous benefits in an order you choose.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 254 Zoo School.

answers.answer: 1. Side Entrance is a unique building placed across two border spaces; unlike ordinary first-building placement, it need not touch an existing building. Other placement rules apply, and later buildings may attach to it. 2. At each break it gives 2 money per adjacent building, excluding empty standard enclosures; it may be adjacent to a kiosk. 3. Side Entrance itself is a unique building, so adjacent kiosks count it for their income. 4. Final reward: 5 appeal with a full map excluding water/rock.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 257 Side Entrance.

answers.answer: 1. Native Farm Animals gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space; water and rock do not count. 2. At game end gain 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately and rounding down per group. 3. Upgrade-restricted empty spaces count even if Build is not upgraded; water/rock spaces are excluded.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 260 Native Farm Animals.

answers.answer: 1. Explorer gives 2 money per different continent or animal-category icon immediately; research icons do not count. 2. Each continent/category type newly introduced gives 1 appeal and 2 money. 3. A double of the same newly introduced icon gives the novelty benefit only once.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 262 Explorer.

answers.answer: 1. WAZA Large Animal Program lets you place a size-5 standard enclosure free under normal placement rules. 2. When playing a large animal, ignore one left-side condition, such as one required icon or the Animals-upgrade condition; terrain requirements cannot be ignored. 3. It stacks with Research Institute, allowing two conditions to be ignored.
answers.evidence: Base Sponsor reference, 263 WAZA Large Animal Program.

answers.answer: 1. Biodiverse Zoo compares your number of icons in each animal category with the player to your right; gain 1 conservation for each category where yours is greater. 2. If that player has none in a category, one of yours is enough to exceed them. 3. Maximum reward is 4 conservation.
answers.evidence: Base Final Scoring and map clarifications: Biodiverse Zoo (009).

answers.answer: 1. Observation Tower applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to the tower hex itself, not merely another rock hex. 2. Special enclosures do not qualify. 3. Housing an animal there gives the two appeal again after an earlier animal was released and the enclosure emptied. 4. The tower is not a building for kiosk income.
answers.evidence: Map 1, Observation Tower clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Outdoor Areas applies to a standard enclosure touching its Outdoor Area hex, not just any water hex. 2. After placement, that enclosure counts as two spaces larger for all purposes; e.g. physical size 2 counts as size 4. 3. This cannot be ignored on release or transfer. 4. It does not affect special enclosures, and Outdoor Area is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 2, Outdoor Areas clarification.

answers.answer: 1. A building on the space adjacent to Commercial Harbor activates it; the first building may begin beside the Harbor but need not. 2. Its discard ability may be used once per own turn, before/during/after your action, never during breaks or another player's turn. 3. The Harbor is not a building.
answers.evidence: Map 4, Commercial Harbor clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Park Restaurant break income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, not per building; empty enclosures qualify and multiple adjacent spaces of one building count separately. 2. The Restaurant is not a building and gives adjacent kiosks no income, though kiosks count other qualifying neighbors normally. 3. Its special-enclosure placement bonus grants either one Reptile House or one Large Bird Aviary free, even before Build II; choose one, not both, and follow other normal placement rules.
answers.evidence: Map 5, Park Restaurant: own income, kiosk income, special-enclosure bonus.

answers.answer: 1. Cover Hollywood Hills H spaces with buildings under ordinary placement rules. Each covered H reveals deck cards until a Sponsor appears; keep it and discard the others. 2. H is not a placement bonus and does not trigger Archaeologist. 3. After all three are covered, every Sponsor's level is one lower. 4. Bonus partner zoos still require Association II for the third/fourth partner, and bonus buildings still require Build II to cover upgrade-marked spaces.
answers.evidence: Map 8, Hollywood Hills clarification.

answers.answer: 1. Pay money equal to the Sponsor's level and meet its usual play conditions. 2. This bonus permits playing the Sponsor only from hand, even if Sponsors II is upgraded; it cannot come from display. 3. The Sponsors Action card remains in its current slot and does not move.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: paid-Sponsor bonus costs level, conditions, hand only, Sponsors card does not move.

answers.answer: 1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; gains beyond those track ends are lost.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: Appeal cannot exceed 113, nor conservation 41; excess gains lost.

answers.answer: 1. Venom targets every other zoo with greater appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal. Hypnosis targets a highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal, with the acting player choosing among ties; copy only slot 1, 2 or 3. 2. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-appeal zoo (at least 5); Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal and most-conservation zoos, with each at least 5 appeal and the conservation leader at least 1 conservation. The acting player chooses among ties for each selection; self-targeting has no effect. 3. Constriction targets every other zoo with at least 5 appeal that is ahead on appeal and/or conservation. Ahead on one track gets one token on its slot-5 card; ahead on both gets one each on its slot-4 and slot-5 cards.
answers.evidence: Interactive target reference and detailed rules for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering, Constriction.

answers.answer: 1. An animal partner-zoo condition requires a partner zoo from the named continent; a Sponsor partner-zoo condition permits any continent. 2. A red maximum-25 appeal condition allows play only while you have at most 25 appeal; its marker is a reminder, not a general cap. 3. A minimum-reputation condition requires at least the printed reputation. 4. A minus-one-condition effect ignores one left-edge requirement; other conditions remain and terrain requirements are not waived.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: partner conditions, max-25, minimum reputation and minus-one-condition.

answers.answer: 1. The illustrated Crested Porcupine's Digging 2 gives up to two selections. 2. For each selection choose either discard a display card (immediately replenish it) or discard a hand card then draw one card from the deck; the two selections may use different options.
answers.evidence: Digging 2 clarification: choose up to twice between display discard/replenish and hand discard/deck draw; decide again after each.

answers.answer: 1. After display cards are taken, move higher-numbered cards down while preserving their order, then fill every empty folder from the deck. 2. On a Digging display discard, higher folders shift down and a deck card fills folder 6 immediately. 3. At a break, discard folders 1 and 2, move remaining cards down, and refill the display.
answers.evidence: Reputation track: move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping order), then fill empty spaces; Digging and break refill rules.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosures empty side up, showing the yellow border and size number. 2. Each placement-bonus space covered is awarded immediately once; turning an enclosure occupied later does not award that placement bonus again.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: standard enclosure empty side up; covered placement bonus immediately once; no second award on occupation.

answers.answer: 1. When the 10-conservation milestone is first reached, each player chooses one Final Scoring card and discards it face down under the remaining Final Scoring pile. 2. The summary specifies face down and under the pile; it does not specify a separate rotational orientation.
answers.evidence: Conservation track: all players choose and discard one Final Scoring card face down under remaining pile.

answers.answer: 1. Randomly determine the starting player; turns proceed clockwise. 2. Play has no formal rounds: players take turns one at a time. 3. On a regular turn, take one action using one of the five Action cards. Effects or bonuses that grant additional actions are resolved according to their timing rules after the relevant action; named Action/Determination abilities, for example, occur after the Animals action and its card movement.
answers.evidence: Setup: randomly determine start player, clockwise; Overview: no formal rounds; Turn Structure: one action per turn; ability timing clarifications.

answers.answer: 1. If no player reaches 10 conservation before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins. 2. The summary does not specify an orientation or destination for these cards in this no-milestone case.
answers.evidence: Conservation track: if no one reaches 10 before game ends, all discard one Final Scoring card before scoring begins. The orientation/destination is specified only for the 10-point milestone.
